explanations.explanation: Pure lips it is, friend. The LORD says, "For then I will restore pure lips to the peoples, that all may call upon the name of the LORD and serve Him shoulder to shoulder." (Zephaniah 3:9) Notice the "all." He's not restoring this for a few folks in the front row. It's for the peoples.

Strong cities are a fair guess, since restoring sounds like rebuilding. But the text says the LORD restores pure lips to the peoples (Zephaniah 3:9). It's about what comes out of mouths. The reason given is so that all may call upon the name of the LORD and serve Him shoulder to shoulder.

Rich harvests would be nice, and my pantry would approve. But the LORD says He will restore pure lips to the peoples (Zephaniah 3:9). So the restoring here is about speech, not crops. The purpose is that all may call upon the name of the LORD.

True! The LORD says, "From beyond the rivers of Cush My worshipers, My scattered people, will bring Me an offering." (Zephaniah 3:10) Cush is a land south of Egypt, so that is a LONG way off. Even from way out there, His scattered people come bringing something to Him.

This one is actually true, friend. The LORD says, "From beyond the rivers of Cush My worshipers, My scattered people, will bring Me an offering." (Zephaniah 3:10) Cush is a land south of Egypt. Far away, scattered, and still bringing an offering.

I'd have bet on True too, so let me set it straight. The LORD says, "On that day you will not be put to shame for any of the deeds by which you have transgressed against Me." (Zephaniah 3:11) Those words say there is no shame on that day for any of those deeds.

False is right, and what a line this is. The LORD says, "On that day you will not be put to shame for any of the deeds by which you have transgressed against Me." (Zephaniah 3:11) Not for some of the deeds. ANY of them. I'd have been ready to sweat through the whole apron, and the text says no shame.

Pride, yes. The LORD says, "…I will remove from among you those who rejoice in their pride, and you will never again be haughty on My holy mountain." (Zephaniah 3:11) Haughty means looking down on everybody. The ones who rejoice in their pride are the ones He takes out of the batch.

Wealth isn't the word here. The text says the LORD will remove "…those who rejoice in their pride…" (Zephaniah 3:11) Nothing in the verse is about money. It says they will never again be haughty on His holy mountain.

Wisdom is a good thing to hold onto, so no worries on that one. But the verse says the LORD will remove "…those who rejoice in their pride…" (Zephaniah 3:11) Pride is the word that fills the blank. After that, they will never again be haughty on His holy mountain.

A meek and humble people, yes! The LORD says, "But I will leave within you a meek and humble people, and they will trust in the name of the LORD." (Zephaniah 3:12) The proud are removed, and the humble are the ones left standing. They are exactly who He keeps.

An army sounds like a strong plan, I know. But the LORD says, "…I will leave within you a meek and humble people…" (Zephaniah 3:12) Meek and humble, not mighty and fearless. And what marks them is that they trust in the name of the LORD.

A council in fancy robes is a good guess for a fancy plan. But the text says the LORD will leave "…a meek and humble people…" (Zephaniah 3:12) No mention of wisdom or wealth in that verse. What it does say is that they will trust in the name of the LORD.
Trust is the word. "…they will trust in the name of the LORD." (Zephaniah 3:12) The meek and humble people lean on Him. They are not leaning on themselves.

Swear is close in spirit, since it's also a word about names. But the verse says the meek and humble people "…will trust in the name of the LORD." (Zephaniah 3:12) Trust is what fills the blank. It's about leaning on Him.

Boast is the opposite energy, friend. The people the LORD leaves are meek and humble, and "…they will trust in the name of the LORD." (Zephaniah 3:12) Boasting belongs with the proud who get removed. Trusting belongs with the humble who stay.

Feed and lie down, yes. The text says, "But they will feed and lie down, with no one to make them tremble." (Zephaniah 3:13) Eat, then rest. I'd call that a pretty good day, and nobody's making them shake.

Standing guard is what you do when you figure trouble is coming. The text says, "But they will feed and lie down, with no one to make them tremble." (Zephaniah 3:13) Nobody is making them tremble, so there's no night shift in this picture. Feeding and lying down is the whole plan.

Hiding and watching is what you do when somebody's coming for you. The text says, "But they will feed and lie down, with no one to make them tremble." (Zephaniah 3:13) Nobody is making them tremble. Feeding and lying down is the picture.

Their punishment, yes. "The LORD has taken away your punishment; He has turned back your enemy." (Zephaniah 3:15) That's the reason for all the shouting. When a weight like that is lifted, I'd be shouting too.

Land is a fair guess, but it isn't the word here. The text says, "The LORD has taken away your punishment…" (Zephaniah 3:15) He takes something away, and it's the punishment. That's the good news the call is singing about.

Losing a king would be no cause for singing. The call says, "The LORD has taken away your punishment…" and then, "Israel’s King, the LORD, is among you…" (Zephaniah 3:15) The King stays, and the punishment goes.
True! The call says, "Israel’s King, the LORD, is among you; no longer will you fear any harm." (Zephaniah 3:15) The King is right there among His people. That's the reason the fear can go.
This one is true, friend. The call says, "Israel’s King, the LORD, is among you; no longer will you fear any harm." (Zephaniah 3:15) The King is named, and He is among them. No more fear of harm.

explanations.answer: The LORD is among you and mighty to save
explanations.explanation: That's it! "The LORD your God is among you; He is mighty to save." (Zephaniah 3:17) The reason not to fear isn't a wall or an army. It's WHO is with them. And He is right in the middle of them.

explanations.answer: Your walls are rebuilt and standing strong
explanations.explanation: Walls feel safe, I get it. But the reason given is, "The LORD your God is among you; He is mighty to save." (Zephaniah 3:17) The text names no walls there. The comfort is the LORD Himself.

explanations.answer: Your army is gathered and ready for battle
explanations.explanation: An army would calm a few nerves, sure. But the call says, "The LORD your God is among you; He is mighty to save." (Zephaniah 3:17) No army is named. The reason not to fear is that He is with them and He saves.

Quiet, yes. "He will quiet you with His love…" (Zephaniah 3:17) After all that talk of fear in this passage, I think that sounds like a gift. The same verse says, "He will rejoice over you with singing." Rejoicing, gladness and singing are all in that one verse.
Test is a fair guess, but the verse says, "He will quiet you with His love…" (Zephaniah 3:17) Quiet is the word that fills the blank. It's a love that settles them, with rejoicing right alongside it.
A warning would be a very different mood. The verse says the LORD "…will quiet you with His love…" (Zephaniah 3:17) Quiet is the word. It sits right next to "He will rejoice over you with gladness…"

explanations.answer: Those who grieve over the appointed feasts
explanations.explanation: Yes, those are the ones. The LORD says, "I will gather those among you who grieve over the appointed feasts, so that you will no longer suffer reproach." (Zephaniah 3:18) The ones who are hurting get gathered. And the reproach stops.

explanations.answer: Those who rejoice in their pride
explanations.explanation: Those are the ones who get removed, not gathered. Back in verse 11 the LORD says, "…I will remove from among you those who rejoice in their pride…" (Zephaniah 3:11) Here He says, "I will gather those among you who grieve over the appointed feasts…" (Zephaniah 3:18)

explanations.answer: Those who rule over the nations
explanations.explanation: Ruling over nations isn't in this verse. The LORD says, "I will gather those among you who grieve over the appointed feasts, so that you will no longer suffer reproach." (Zephaniah 3:18) He gathers the grieving ones. And their reproach ends.

Lame, yes, and that's the word. The LORD says, "I will save the lame and gather the scattered…" (Zephaniah 3:19) He names the lame right there in the promise, next to the scattered. He says plainly that He will save them.

The proud are on the other list. Earlier the LORD says He will remove those who rejoice in their pride (Zephaniah 3:11). In this verse He says, "I will save the lame and gather the scattered…" (Zephaniah 3:19)

The mighty seem like the easy ones to pick. But the LORD says, "I will save the lame and gather the scattered…" (Zephaniah 3:19) It's the lame He names. He is the one who will save them, and the scattered get gathered too.

That's the opposite of what He says, friend. The LORD says, "…I will appoint praise and fame for the disgraced throughout the earth." (Zephaniah 3:19) Praise and fame, not hiding. And it reaches throughout the earth.

False, and what a turnaround. The LORD says, "…I will appoint praise and fame for the disgraced throughout the earth." (Zephaniah 3:19) The disgraced are not hidden away. They get praise and fame, all across the earth.

Their captives, yes. The LORD says, "…I will give you fame and praise among all the peoples of the earth when I restore your captives before your very eyes…" (Zephaniah 3:20) Before their very eyes! They get to watch it happen.

A temple is a sensible guess, but it isn't in this verse. The LORD says, "…when I restore your captives before your very eyes…" (Zephaniah 3:20) It's the captives He restores. And He does it right where His people can see.

A kingdom would be a big restoration, I'll give you that. But the verse says, "…when I restore your captives before your very eyes…" says the LORD. (Zephaniah 3:20) Captives is the word. And they'd see it with their own eyes.
